course: AP Psychology — all five units, taught as the method of a conviction review: what an eye can resolve, what a memory does between the event and the question, how an identification procedure is built, and what a number about a person is entitled to claim
curriculum: Acuity as an angle: what the eye can resolve falls off with distance
Illuminance, and the light a scene actually had
Rods, cones and scotopic vision: what the dark takes away
Dark adaptation, and how long the eye takes to arrive
Selective attention: attending is choosing, and choosing costs
Inattentional blindness: looking at is not seeing
Weapon focus, and what an arousing object does to a description
Encoding: memory is built at the moment, from what was attended to
Storage and forgetting: the curve is steep at the start
Retrieval is reconstruction, not playback
Source monitoring: keeping the fact and losing where it came from
The misinformation effect: what arrives after the event gets in
Co-witness contamination: two accounts that have met are one account
The cross-race effect in identification
Flashbulb memory: vivid, confident, and no more accurate
Arousal and encoding: the amygdala, cortisol and the inverted U
Sleep deprivation and the loss of cognitive control
Suggestibility, repeated questioning and the child witness
How a lineup is built: fillers, and the ones nobody would pick
Functional size: how many of them were real alternatives
Simultaneous against sequential presentation
Double-blind administration, and expectancy
Post-identification feedback and confidence inflation
Confidence and accuracy: a relationship that survives only at the moment
Signal detection: sensitivity against where the line is set
Base rates: what a match is worth depends on who is in the pool
Reliability: the same measurement twice, and two people measuring once
Validity, standardization and norms: what a score is compared against
Experimenter and investigator expectancy, and the control that removes it
False confession: minimisation, maximisation and the innocent person's arithmetic

distance from the source, in metres

how many mock witnesses were asked, having read only the description
how many of them picked the suspect without ever having seen the crime

equations.about: sensitivity — telling apart, separated from willingness to choose
symbols: sensitivity, the distance between the two distributions in standard units
the hit rate turned into a standard score
the false-alarm rate turned into a standard score

symbols: the odds that the identified person is the offender, after the identification
the odds before it, from the pool of people who could have been there
the likelihood ratio — how much more often an identification like this one comes from the offender than from an innocent person

symbols: the standard score, in standard deviations
the mean of the norm group
the standard deviation of the norm group
